item.title: Saudi Arabia receives conjoined Fijian twins for possible separation surgery
item.description: Conjoined Fijian twins Jesibel and Desisia arrived in Riyadh on Friday under directives from Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman to undergo evaluation for a possible separation surgery. The twins and their family arrived at King Khalid International Airport before being transferred to King Abdullah Specialist Children’s Hospital und
item.content:encoded:
Conjoined Fijian twins Jesibel and Desisia arrived in Riyadh on Friday under directives from Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman to undergo evaluation for a possible separation surgery.

The twins and their family arrived at King Khalid International Airport before being transferred to King Abdullah Specialist Children’s Hospital under the Ministry of National Guard Health Affairs, where a specialized medical team will assess their condition and determine whether separation surgery is feasible.

Dr. Abdullah Al Rabeeah, supervisor general of the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) and head of the Saudi Conjoined Twins Program’s medical and surgical team, thanked the Kingdom’s leadership for the humanitarian initiative, describing it as a reflection of Saudi Arabia’s commitment to providing medical assistance to people in need regardless of nationality or background.

Al Rabeeah said the Saudi Conjoined Twins Program has become a global leader in treating some of the world’s most complex cases, attributing its success to the Kingdom’s humanitarian vision and the expertise of its specialized medical teams.

The twins’ family expressed their gratitude to the Saudi leadership and people for the warm reception and hospitality they received, as well as for the swift response in providing their daughters with specialized medical care.

item.title: TLTB says freehold Momi land Should revert if deal cannot be completed
item.description: The iTaukei Land Trust Board (TLTB) says it remains committed to resolving the long-running Momi Land Swap, maintaining that if the original agreement cannot be lawfully completed, the affected freehold land should revert to iTaukei ownership. In a statement responding to growing public discussion on social media, TLTB said it is pursuing a lawful resolution, either by completing the land swap app
item.content:encoded:
The iTaukei Land Trust Board (TLTB) says it remains committed to resolving the long-running Momi Land Swap, maintaining that if the original agreement cannot be lawfully completed, the affected freehold land should revert to iTaukei ownership.

In a statement responding to growing public discussion on social media, TLTB said it is pursuing a lawful resolution, either by completing the land swap approved by Cabinet in 2006 or by reversing the transaction to restore the original ownership arrangements.

The Momi Land Swap was approved by Cabinet on 4 July 2006 to facilitate the development of the Momi Bay tourism project, now home to the Fiji Marriott Resort Momi Bay.

The arrangement involved the conversion of 68.7 hectares (170 acres) of iTaukei land owned by Tokatoka Nasau into freehold land, in exchange for an equivalent area of freehold land owned by Matapo Limited, which was to be converted into iTaukei land. That freehold land was later acquired by the Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF).

TLTB said the project has generated significant benefits for landowners and surrounding communities, with more than $5.2 million paid to Tokatoka Nasau and the Vanua o Nalolo through lease premiums, rental payments, scholarships, community projects, compensation and infrastructure assistance.

The Board said the landowners also receive annual lease payments, currently $260,000, subject to five-yearly reviews, while their company operates a tours and transfers business servicing the Marriott Resort with a fleet of 19 vehicles. The lease also provides employment and training preferences for landowners.

However, TLTB said the final stage of the land swap was never completed.

While freehold titles were transferred to TLTB in 2007, one title was later mortgaged to the Fiji Development Bank before being transferred to FNPF in 2008.

According to TLTB, Government intervention at the time prevented the final conversion of the freehold land into iTaukei land.

The Board said it has pursued the matter for years and made a formal submission to Government last year proposing that the land swap be unwound if completion proved impossible.

TLTB said discussions are continuing with the Ministry of Lands and FNPF to resolve the issue.

However, it noted that Section 29(5) of the Constitution prevents the direct conversion of freehold land into iTaukei land, creating the principal legal obstacle to completing the original agreement.

As a result, TLTB said neither Government nor any other institution has the authority to simply reclassify freehold land as iTaukei land, regardless of the intentions behind the original arrangement.

The Board said once the required acquisition and transmission process is completed by the Director of Lands, the land would become eligible for registration as iTaukei land under existing legal requirements before a new Register of iTaukei Land could be created for Tokatoka Nasau.

TLTB said the affected landowners have consistently maintained that only two outcomes would be acceptable.

Either the original land swap approved by Cabinet in 2006 should be completed, or, if that can no longer be achieved within the law, the original iTaukei land should be returned.

The Board said it remains committed to working with all parties to reach a lawful and fair resolution that protects the interests of the landowners.

item.title: FRCS warns of fake tax clearance certificates in circulation
item.description: The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) is warning businesses, government agencies and the public about the circulation of fraudulent Tax Clearance and Tax Compliance Certificates, along with fake letters falsely claiming legitimate certificates have been cancelled due to system errors. FRCS said the documents are fraudulent, unauthorised and were not issued by the Service.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) is warning businesses, government agencies and the public about the circulation of fraudulent Tax Clearance and Tax Compliance Certificates, along with fake letters falsely claiming legitimate certificates have been cancelled due to system errors.

FRCS said the documents are fraudulent, unauthorised and were not issued by the Service.

The agency warned that producing, distributing, possessing or using fake tax documents may constitute serious criminal offences under Fiji’s laws and could result in substantial fines, imprisonment or both.

FRCS is urging businesses, government ministries, statutory bodies, financial institutions, procurement entities and members of the public to independently verify the authenticity of any tax certificate before relying on it for official purposes.

The Service also clarified that it does not cancel or revoke Tax Clearance or Tax Compliance Certificates through informal emails, third-party correspondence or unverified letters. Any changes to a certificate’s status are reflected only through FRCS’s official systems and can be verified using its online certificate validation portal.

FRCS Chief Executive Officer Udit Singh said the circulation of fake certificates is a deliberate attempt to deceive businesses, government agencies and the public.

“The circulation of fake tax certificates and fraudulent cancellation notices is a deliberate attempt to deceive businesses, government agencies, and the public. FRCS will not tolerate any activity that compromises the integrity of our systems and processes.”

Mr Singh urged organisations and individuals not to accept tax certificates at face value and to verify them through official FRCS channels.

He advised organisations that identify suspicious documents to retain a copy, suspend the relevant transaction and immediately report the matter to FRCS together with details of the individual or entity that submitted the document.

Mr Singh also warned that FRCS will work closely with law enforcement agencies to investigate and prosecute anyone involved in producing, distributing or using fraudulent tax documents.

The Service is encouraging anyone who receives a suspicious tax certificate or cancellation notice to report it immediately.

item.title: Remittances climb to record $875M, RBF reports
item.description: Remittance inflows to Fiji continued their strong upward trend, rising 26.3 per cent to $875.2 million in the year to June, according to the Reserve Bank of Fiji’s latest July Economic Review. The RBF said remittance outflows also increased, rising 15 per cent to $293.7 million over the same period.
item.content:encoded:
Remittance inflows to Fiji continued their strong upward trend, rising 26.3 per cent to $875.2 million in the year to June, according to the Reserve Bank of Fiji’s latest July Economic Review.

The RBF said remittance outflows also increased, rising 15 per cent to $293.7 million over the same period.

As a result, net remittances grew by 32.9 per cent to $581.5 million, reflecting stronger growth in money sent into Fiji than funds transferred overseas.

The central bank attributed the sustained increase in inward remittances to Fiji’s expanding diaspora, continued participation in overseas employment schemes and improved access to digital and fintech-based remittance services.

Meanwhile, the increase in outward remittances was linked to the growing number of migrant workers residing in Fiji.

The RBF said the continued growth in remittances remains an important source of foreign exchange and household income, supporting economic activity across the country.

item.title: Sayed-Khaiyum says Attorney-General must protect judiciary from public attacks
item.description: Former Attorney-General Aiyaz Sayed-Khaiyum says it is the responsibility of the Acting Attorney-General to protect Fiji’s judiciary from public attacks that could undermine confidence in the courts. In a social media post, Sayed-Khaiyum said more than a month had passed since a politician published what he described as disparaging comments and a video targeting Chief Justice Sailesi Temo followin
item.content:encoded:
Former Attorney-General Aiyaz Sayed-Khaiyum says it is the responsibility of the Acting Attorney-General to protect Fiji’s judiciary from public attacks that could undermine confidence in the courts.

In a social media post, Sayed-Khaiyum said more than a month had passed since a politician published what he described as disparaging comments and a video targeting Chief Justice Sailesi Temo following the judgment in the State v Aiyaz Sayed-Khaiyum and Mohammed Saneem case on 26 June 2026.

He claimed the comments amounted to contempt of court and questioned why no legal action had been taken.

“The obvious person who can immediately and effectively do something tangible about it is the Attorney-General, in our situation the Acting Attorney General,” Sayed-Khaiyum said.

He argued that safeguarding the independence and integrity of the judiciary is a core responsibility of the Attorney-General.

“It is the absolute responsibility of the Attorney-General to safeguard the Honourable Chief Justice, any member of the judiciary, the judiciary as a whole from being attacked, maligned and threatened by any member of the public.”

Sayed-Khaiyum said contemptuous remarks erode public confidence in the justice system.

“Contemptuous comments undermine the standing of the judiciary. A standing that is critically necessary to ensure that the sanctity of the workings and independence of the judiciary is maintained unhindered and respected by all,” he said.

He said the legal test for contempt is whether comments create a real risk of undermining the authority, integrity and impartiality of the courts in the eyes of a fair-minded and reasonable member of the public.

Sayed-Khaiyum also questioned whether the Acting Attorney-General’s response would have differed had criticism of the judiciary come from another group.

“The Acting Attorney-General needs to understand that applying the law, and in this case protecting the judiciary, must be above his political and personal views and proclivities. He needs to apply and practice the law impartially,” he said.

While acknowledging that court decisions can be criticised through legal analysis or appealed through the courts, Sayed-Khaiyum said there was a clear distinction between legitimate criticism and personal attacks on judges.

“You cannot malign a judge or the Judiciary as a whole just because you don’t like the decision of the Court,” he said.

Sayed-Khaiyum urged the Acting Attorney-General to immediately commence contempt proceedings, arguing that protecting the judiciary and preserving public confidence in the administration of justice must take precedence over political considerations.

item.title: Seruiratu calls for review of health workers’ maritime transport
item.description: Leader of the Opposition Inia Seruiratu has called on the Government to urgently review transport arrangements for healthcare workers serving Fiji’s rural and maritime communities following the rescue of six health workers who went missing in Lau waters. Mr Seruiratu expressed relief that the six healthcare workers had been found safe and thanked all those involved in the search and rescue operati
item.content:encoded:
Leader of the Opposition Inia Seruiratu has called on the Government to urgently review transport arrangements for healthcare workers serving Fiji’s rural and maritime communities following the rescue of six health workers who went missing in Lau waters.

Mr Seruiratu expressed relief that the six healthcare workers had been found safe and thanked all those involved in the search and rescue operation.

“My sincere thanks go to the Republic of Fiji Navy, the crew of Lomaiviti Princess 12 and all government agencies, search teams, mariners and communities whose tireless efforts brought this search to a successful end. This outcome is a testament to the courage and cooperation of our maritime community,” he said.

However, Mr Seruiratu said the incident should prompt a review of the safety measures in place for frontline workers travelling to the outer islands.

“This incident must also serve as a wake-up call. Our healthcare workers who serve in rural and maritime communities carry out essential, often difficult work far from the resources and support available in urban centres. They deserve nothing less than safe, reliable and accessible transport as they travel to serve our people in the outer islands,” he said.

The Opposition Leader called for an urgent review of transport arrangements, including the provision of seaworthy vessels, appropriate safety equipment, reliable communication systems and emergency contingency plans.

“Our frontline health workers put their lives on the line to serve rural and maritime communities. The least we can do is ensure their journeys to and from these postings are safe,” Mr Seruiratu said.

He also acknowledged the anxiety experienced by the families of the six health workers and said he was thankful they would now be safely reunited with their loved ones.

item.title: Concerns raised over medical team’s sea travel
item.description: A VETERAN seafarer has questioned why frontline medical teams are still being transported in small fibreglass boats decades after government-operated medical vessels once served Fiji’s maritime communities. Operations manager of the inter-island passenger vessel MV Yavirau, Raivolita Uluilakeba raised the concerns in a social media post while reacting to the disappearance of six Ministry of Health
item.content:encoded:
A VETERAN seafarer has questioned why frontline medical teams are still being transported in small fibreglass boats decades after government-operated medical vessels once served Fiji’s maritime communities.

Operations manager of the inter-island passenger vessel MV Yavirau, Raivolita Uluilakeba raised the concerns in a social media post while reacting to the disappearance of six Ministry of Health officials in Lau waters on Wednesday.

The six healthcare workers went missing while travelling by boat on an official outreach mission, prompting a major multi-agency search and rescue operation.

Reflecting on his years with the former Fiji Marine Department in the 1980s, Mr Uluilakeba said medical ships were once strategically stationed across the country to transport medical teams and respond to emergencies.

“Just resting on MV Yavirau at Lakeba, and gazing out to sea with silent hopes for the missing,” Mr Uluilakeba wrote.

“Thinking back, to those days in the Fiji Marines, mid 80s, where I began my seafaring career, the Fiji Marine Department (now GSS) had medical ships stationed around the country, all manned by Fiji Marine Government crew.

“We had MV Vuniwai ni Lau stationed in Lakeba and another stationed in Vanuabalavu, at Levuka we had the Cagi mai Ra.

Mr Uluilakeba said the vessels were specifically designed to support healthcare delivery to Fiji’s maritime islands.

“Their main purpose ??…we’re to standby for medical emergencies and transport medical staff on their frequent tours to their districts.

“These ships could transfer patients, had showers, galley and comfortable beds for medical staff.”

Questioning the current state of maritime health transport, he wrote:

“So here we are decades forward, and our medical staff are still being transported in fibreglass boats.

“Did bringing in a moving eight (8) million dollar hospital ship, MV Veivueti solve the problem?”

item.title: A new era for care
item.description: THE Government has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening childhood cancer care, with a $41million investment in Fiji’s first Radiotherapy and Cancer Treatment Centre and continued support for families battling the disease. Assistant Minister for Health Penioni Ravunawa made the announcement yesterday while speaking at the launch of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, saying improving outcomes f
item.content:encoded:
THE Government has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening childhood cancer care, with a $41million investment in Fiji’s first Radiotherapy and Cancer Treatment Centre and continued support for families battling the disease.

Assistant Minister for Health Penioni Ravunawa made the announcement yesterday while speaking at the launch of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, saying improving outcomes for young patients required a stronger and more resilient health system.

“The ministry remains committed to strengthening early diagnosis, improving referral pathways, expanding specialist services and ensuring children have access to quality treatment regardless of where they live,” he said.

“Reliable information is equally important.

“Strengthening cancer registration and data collection enables us to better understand disease patterns, plan services effectively and continue improving patient outcomes.”

Mr Ravunawa said Government remained committed to improving cancer care through increased investment and partnerships.

“We are proud to support WOWS Kids Fiji through a $100,000 Government grant, assisting the organisation to continue delivering practical support to children and families across Fiji.

“In addition, the 2026–2027 National Budget includes $41million towards establishing Fiji’s first Radiotherapy and Cancer Treatment Centre.

“This represents one of the most significant investments in cancer care in our nation’s history.

“For many families, it will mean improved access to specialised treatment closer to home and reduced financial and emotional hardship.”

He said Government could not tackle childhood cancer alone, stressing that success depended on partnerships with organisations such as WOWS Kids Fiji, healthcare professionals, communities, churches, schools, businesses and development partners.
